industries.outcomes_title: What the radios do on site

horeca.name: HoReCa
horeca.desc: Hotels, restaurants, events. Discreet earpieces, clean channels.
horeca.problem: Staff loses contact across noisy floors and between levels. Guests overhear crew chatter.
horeca.solution: Small radios and concealed earpieces. Only the staff hear it, and no frequency permit is needed.
pains: Waiters can’t hear the kitchen at peak hours
Regular phones die halfway through a shift

outcomes.l: Up to 6 floors of coverage — Motorola CLP 446 and CLK 446
Radio weight: invisible under a uniform, headset in the box
The free 446 MHz band — no permit needed

horeca.quote: Guests no longer hear what’s happening in the kitchen. Shifts got calmer and turnover went up — the team clears tables faster.

faq.q: Do we need a frequency permit?
faq.a: No. These radios work on the free 446 MHz band, so there is nothing to register.

faq.q: How many radios for a restaurant?
faq.a: Usually four to six: the host, the floor manager, the chef, the barista, a waiter and the store room. We will come out and count for free.

faq.q: Can I try before I buy?
faq.a: Yes — free test on your site.

horeca.h1: Two-way radios for hotels and restaurants
horeca.meta_desc: Two-way radios for hotels, restaurants and events in Tashkent. Motorola CLP 446 and CLK 446: up to 7,400 m² of coverage, 68 g, earpiece in the box. Free trial.

construction.name: Construction
construction.desc: Massive sites. IP67 ruggedness, long-range coverage.
construction.problem: Dust, vibration, kilometers between crews. Regular phones don’t survive and don’t cover the site.
construction.solution: Rugged IP67 DMR radios: RCD-70 PRO on site, RCD-50 and RCD-60 PRO for the crews.
pains: Foreman can’t reach crane ops or fitters
Phones crack, drown, die in dust
Cell signal vanishes past concrete walls

outcomes.l: Dust and water on site — RCD-70 PRO
Clear digital audio over site noise — RCD-50, RCD-60 and RCD-70 PRO

construction.quote: We used to lose 2 hours a day chasing foremen. Now — press a button, the whole shift hears it. Paid off in a month.

faq.a: IP67 keeps out the dust, grit and water jets of a site. The exact temperature range depends on the model — we will bring radios to your site and test them in your conditions before you buy.
Only if the site runs longer than 500 m, or there are floors between the crews. We assess that on the visit, free of charge.

faq.q: What if a radio ends up in wet concrete?
faq.a: IP67 withstands dust and water jets. If a radio does fail, we repair or replace it under the 12-month warranty in our own service centre.

construction.meta_desc: Radios for building sites in Tashkent: the RCD-70 PRO has IP67 dust and water protection, reaches 10 km in the open, and stays clear through site noise.

security.name: Security
security.problem: You need a channel nobody can listen in on, an alarm button, and a map showing every post.
security.solution: Digital radios with encryption, an alarm button and GPS. The dispatcher sees every post on a map.
pains: Officers go off the radar — nobody knows where
Open frequencies can be scanned by anyone
The alarm goes up by phone — that costs 30 to 90 seconds

outcomes.l: Only your own team hears you — RCD-50, RCD-60 and RCD-70 PRO
You can see where each post is — RCD-70 PRO
In dense urban blocks — RCD-70 PRO

security.quote: We standardized on encrypted DMR across all our sites. Dispatch sees every officer, and the panic button has already saved us twice.

faq.q: Can anyone listen in on us?
faq.a: Practically not: in digital mode the conversation is encrypted, and the key can be changed from software.

faq.q: Does GPS work inside a building?
faq.a: Outdoors, yes. Indoors the radio shows the last point where it had a signal.

faq.q: Where does the alarm button send its signal?
faq.a: To everyone on the channel and to the dispatcher, together with the post's coordinates.

security.meta_desc: Radios for security teams in Tashkent: AES-256 encryption, an alarm button, GPS on the RCD-70 PRO and up to 3 km through built-up streets. 12-month warranty.

mining.name: Mining · Oil · Gas
mining.problem: Huge areas, hazardous zones, strict intrinsic-safety requirements.
mining.solution: Digital RCD PRO radios with IP67 protection, encryption and a shift-long battery. We size the kit to the site.
pains: 3 km pit — regular radios can’t reach across
Standard electronics banned in Ex zones
Underground crew loses contact with surface

outcomes.l: Dust and water on site — RCD-70 PRO
Only your own team hears you — the RCD PRO range
A full shift on one charge — RCD-70 and RCD-50 PRO

mining.quote: Radiocom rolled out the DMR network across the pit in 3 days. Second winter running — zero downtime.

faq.a: There are no intrinsically safe (Ex) versions in the current catalogue. Tell us which class your site requires and we will source it separately.

faq.q: Do the frequencies have to be registered?
faq.a: Yes, and we do it for you: we handle the whole filing with State Comms of Uzbekistan.
12 months on the radio unit. Servicing is done in our authorised centre with original parts.

mining.meta_desc: Two-way radios for mining, oil and gas: IP67 against dust and water, AES-256 encryption, a 3600 mAh battery that lasts a shift. ERIELL and ENTER Engineering.

transport.name: Transport · Logistics
transport.problem: The dispatcher loses drivers outside the city. Cellular is expensive and drops.
transport.solution: Radiocom RCD radios in the vehicles. Out of town — PoC radios: they run over the mobile network, so you have coverage across the whole country.
pains: Driver in Bukhara — Tashkent dispatch can’t reach
Convoy comms via phone speakerphone only

outcomes.l: The dispatcher sees the crew on a map — RCD-70 PRO
On the road and in open ground — RCD-70, RCD-60 and RCD-50 PRO
A shift behind the wheel without recharging — RCD-70 and RCD-50 PRO

transport.quote: We moved the whole fleet onto radios that work over the mobile network — we pay 40% less for communications, and the dispatcher sees every driver on a map.

faq.q: Will there be coverage on the highway and in the mountains?
faq.a: Wherever the mobile network reaches, yes. For a specific route, check the coverage with your own operator.

faq.q: Can we combine them with normal radios?
faq.a: Yes. A gateway goes in the dispatch room and both kinds of radio share one channel.

transport.h1: Two-way radios for transport and logistics
transport.meta_desc: Radios for transport and logistics: the dispatcher sees every crew on a map, up to 10 km on the highway, 3600 mAh for a shift at the wheel. Free trial.

manufacturing.name: Manufacturing · Warehousing
manufacturing.problem: Shifts across many zones, industrial noise, foremen need instant coordination.
manufacturing.solution: Digital radios with a repeater: everyone hears everyone, anywhere on the site. Plus warehouse terminals with a scanner for stock-keeping.
pains: Foremen can’t hear each other over machine noise
Store staff run between the racks with paper
Shift doesn’t know what happened at another zone

outcomes.l: Digital voice without interference — the RCD PRO range
Across shop floors and yards — RCD-50 and RCD-60 PRO
Your own frequency: no subscription, no traffic charges

manufacturing.quote: The radios and the warehouse terminals were running in a week. The store staff stopped walking around with notebooks and picking got almost twice as fast.

faq.q: Do radios work in noisy shops?
faq.a: Yes. Noise cancelling strips out the background — you can hear at 100 dB on the shop floor.

faq.q: Do the warehouse terminals work with 1C?
faq.a: Yes. There are ready-made integrations, and we write to fit your own stock system where needed.
2 to 7 days depending on plant size.
